newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines shopping around for planes, ships.
newsitem.headline: Philippines shopping around for planes, ships.

text.p: The Philippines is shopping around for 24 "slightly used" fighter jets and a dozen ships to beef up its fighting capability under a $2-billion military modernisation programme, officials said on Tuesday.
Armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said the military had sent missions to Europe, Asia and the United States to evaluate offers from potential suppliers.

Philippine officials last week stressed the need to speed up the modernisation programme following two incidents last month involving alleged incursions by Chinese vessels into areas claimed by Manila in the South China Sea.

Beijing says all islands in the South China Sea, including the potentially oil-rich Spratly Islands, historically belong to China. The Spratlys are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, the Philippines, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei.
"The modest modernisation programme will give us more capability to fulfill our mandate to protect our territorial integrity," Acedera told a news conference.
He said the Philippines was looking at buying second-hand equipment.
"It's like a buying a car. You get a brand new one but it's a lemon, so it's better to get something slightly used but tried and tested," he said.
Among planes the Philippines was looking at were U.S.-made F-16s and F-18s and Russian-made MiG-29s, Acedera said. The navy was interested in buying 10 patrol boats and two frigates.
The government has given top priority to upgrading its obselete navy and air force equipment.
Acedera declined to say if the decision to speed up the modernisation programme was prompted by worries about Chinese intentions in the Spratlys.
The Philippines in April accused China of sending armed naval ships near islands claimed by Manila in the Spratlys. Beijing said they were research vessels on a scientific mission.
Later in the month, Philippine navy patrol boats shooed away a Chinese Bureau of Fisheries ship reportedly carrying radio ham operators near a Manila-claimed shoal off Subic freeport.
Fishermen later hoisted the Philippine flag on the shoal, prompting protests from China.
